timeline.title: A Short History of Birthdays
items: Romans marked the birthdays of friends and family with feasts, gifts and wishes for good luck.
In Germany, children's birthday parties called Kinderfeste had a cake with a candle for every year.
Sisters Mildred and Patty Hill published Good Morning to All. Its melody became Happy Birthday to You.
A judge ruled the old copyright claim on Happy Birthday invalid. Now it belongs to all of us.
today: The most important birthday in the history books. Well, in ours.

letters.title: Wise Words for Your Birthday
items: There is no one alive who is Youer than You.
Dr. Seuss, Happy Birthday to You!, 1959
We do not remember days, we remember moments.
Wrinkles should merely indicate where the smiles have been.
A joy that is shared is a joy made double.
letters.hand: Every one of them is true. Especially the bit about smiles, {who}.

facts.title: The Science of Birthdays
items: Every birthday marks one more trip around the Sun, about 940 million kilometres. Well travelled.
Around twenty million people share your birthday. None of them are quite as good at it as you.
In a room of just 23 people, there is a better than even chance two of them share a birthday.
Happy Birthday to You is often called the most recognised song in the English language.
People born on 29 February only get a true birthday once every four years.
Your skin renews its outer layer every few weeks, so you are always a slightly fresher edition.
facts.hand: Science says you are {age}. We say you are timeless, {who}.

note.title: What we believe a birthday is for
paras: We make magazines for a living, and birthdays are our favourite kind.
We believe a birthday is not really about getting older. It is the one day a year when everyone who loves you is allowed to say so, out loud, without it being strange.
{who}, someone wanted to do exactly that. Not with a card anyone could buy, but with pages full of you: your face, your stories, the little things that make you, you.
That someone is {from}. And from everything they told us, the world got very lucky the day you arrived.
note.wish: Happy birthday, {who}. Here is to you.
